name: Vortex
meaning: Three sweeping currents drawn into one tightly turning spiral.
geometry: One deeply turning organic whirlpool made from THREE thick sweeping currents, all flowing into the same off-center hollow. Their outer ends spread unevenly into a broad fluid outline and their inner curves follow a single common course. Large tapered cutouts separate the currents. It must feel like moving water captured as a carved silhouette, not metal blades, arrowheads, a propeller or a spinning fan. No outer circle. The shared controlled course represents governance directing transformation.

Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a single original civilization pictogram for the LUMINAe science-fantasy strategy game. This is a standalone transparent symbol, NOT a logo mockup, medallion or illustrative scene.

All important cutouts wider than 4% of the emblem width. Simple anatomy, striking silhouette, no decorative microdetail.
ABSOLUTELY EXCLUDE: sculptural rendering, 3D, metal, stone texture, wood texture, engraved surfaces, lighting, bevels, shadows, gradients, color accents, glow, hairlines, distressed speckles, backdrop, checkerboard baked into image, frames, common shields, circular badge borders, letters, names, words, numerals, labels, runes, watermarks. Do not include small secondary icons around the main symbol. Negative space should be truly alpha-transparent, not painted black.

name: Chrysalis
meaning: A hanging cocoon splitting around an emerging wing.
geometry: A recognizable hanging cocoon attached by a short thick stalk, with a curved organic shell splitting open asymmetrically. One broad simple folded butterfly wing emerges through the opening; wing has one generous teardrop-shaped cutout, no veins or speckling. The shell stays dominant, the emerging wing differs clearly from the old enclosed form. Strong upright silhouette, cocoon bulges toward the lower half, wing reaches to one side. No fully emerged butterfly, leaves, surrounding branch or complete insect body.

name: Ouroboros
meaning: A serpent visibly consuming its own tail.
geometry: A single thick-bodied organic serpent curled into an uneven near-circle, its unmistakable simple snake head visibly biting and swallowing its own tapered tail near the upper right. The head is clear from an open jaw notch and broader blunt snout, no tiny eye required; one large inward bite cutout makes self-consumption legible. Body is smooth and substantial, widest at lower left, then gradually tapers around the same continuing loop. Slightly asymmetric hand-carved contour. No scales, horns, fangs, arrowheads, infinity crossing, knot or second snake. Maintain wide transparent center.

name: Mycelium
meaning: A branching fungal network reconnects around a concealed center.
geometry: A recognizable bold fungal root network, low and wide, spreading as five thick organic branching tendrils. Several branches reconnect to make THREE large irregular open cells, showing a coordinated mesh rather than isolated roots. In its off-center middle is one opaque organic root-knot; two tendrils clearly disappear behind it and reappear beyond, concealing their internal connection. Connected coherent silhouette with tapered outward tips. No mushroom cap, top plate, eye, sun, trunk, leaves, brain, circuit nodes, spider, tiny roots or radial starburst. The outline is irregular and laterally spreading, like underground hyphae simplified into a powerful stamp.
